summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. On the raw brief it first said the task was "bounded". After I gave the scripted answer ("it should persist… other forms will need it later"), it switched to "architectural", on its own and explicitly. It then asked clarifying questions, compared approaches, walked through the design in sections, and wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/. It showed me that spec and asked for approval before touching any code. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it moved on to hyperpowers:writing-plans. It wrote no implementation code at any point in the run.
reasoning: All five criteria are met as written, but it's a close call. Claude's first read of the bare brief was "bounded", which is the misclassification this scenario is designed to catch. It only escalated after my scripted scope answer, which the story explicitly allows. From then on it followed the full spec path: it announced the switch, wrote the spec file and asked for review before any code. It never presented an in-chat design as the final approval step, and it never framed the work as a spike. Graded criterion by criterion this is a pass. Whoever aggregates the sibling runs should know the escalation came after clarification, not from the first read of the brief.

observations.description: On the unmodified brief the router said "bounded" ("login() already exists in app.js:4, and this is a signature change in one file"). It escalated only after I confirmed persistence and cross-form reuse. Its first read did not pick up the hints of a public interface change in "add a userId parameter". This matters for the aggregate threshold across the five sibling scenarios.

Codex review of the spec failed. The seeded stub plugin returned an empty payload `{}` for both review lenses, and verdict-normalize reported "incomplete". Claude handled this sensibly: it logged it as an ungated event, clearly told me "The spec has had no Codex review", and did not relaunch. The approach-gate Codex call failed the same way.

Claude said it added a .gitignore for docs/hyperpowers "per your standing instruction". I never gave any such instruction, so it looks like it is acting on an injected config or memory. As a result the spec is not committed, which conflicts with wording elsewhere about a "committed spec file".
Several Claude Code startup dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions) default to "No, exit". One mistaken Enter would quit.

The brainstorming session was long: about 7 questions plus 3 design sections, around 10 minutes, for a brief that sounded like one line. The questions were well reasoned but heavy. Its walk through three possible sources for the userId (caller, response, form field) was good, and it correctly pointed out the brief's premise problem: the client can't know a userId before logging in.

criteria.evidence: Session log, list of tool calls: line 1 is `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`, followed by the text "I'm using the brainstorming skill. Let me look at the codebase before classifying." None of the Write/Edit calls touch app code.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: Log text: "That upgrades the path. Persistence plus reuse across forms that don't exist yet is new structure this repo doesn't have... **Re-classifying as architectural.**" The file docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-client-side-session-identity-design.md (11754 bytes) exists, and the spec itself says "the work was re-classified from a bounded change to an architectural one." Note: the first classification was "bounded"; the switch came after my scripted persistence/reuse answer.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen showed: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-client-side-session-identity-design.md ... Please review the spec and let me know if you want changes before I write out the implementation plan." At that point `git status --short` showed only `?? .gitignore`. Every Write/Edit in the log went to the spec, .gitignore, or ~/.cache codex-review prompt files; none touched app.js, index.html or package.json.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Claude did first say "I'm classifying this as **bounded**... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". It never presented a bounded design for approval, though: it switched to architectural and wrote the spec file. That file is not committed; it added a .gitignore that excludes docs/hyperpowers. It was written and put up for review, so the spec step was not skipped.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present probe plan
criteria.evidence: Searching the log text for architectural|re-?classif|bounded|spec found only bounded→architectural wording. The word 'spike' never appeared and no probe plan was offered.
